summary: Postinstall credential harvester exfiltrating to Telegram Bot API and hardcoded IP
details: package.json declares a postinstall hook ("node index.js || exit 0") that runs automatically on npm install. index.js enumerates the installer's home directory for cloud, CI, and developer credentials (~/.aws/credentials, ~/.ssh private keys, ~/.gcloud, ~/.azure, ~/.npmrc, ~/.yarnrc, ~/.gitconfig, ~/.docker, ~/.kube, ~/.netrc, ~/.pypirc, ~/.gem, ~/.cargo, VSCode settings, Firebase/Vercel/Netlify/Supabase tokens, HuggingFace token) and scans process.env for keys matching TOKEN, KEY, SECRET, PASSWORD, AWS, AZURE, GCP. The harvested data is base64-encoded (index.js line 255) and transmitted (index.js line 310-311) to the Telegram Bot API (api.telegram.org, bot token 8797336493, chat 8814152665) via sendMessage/sendDocument and to a hardcoded IP endpoint at http://2.26.82.63:8888/collect. Prior to exfiltration the code returns early when NODE_ENV=test, CI=true, JEST_WORKER_ID, VITEST are set or /.dockerenv exists, and then sleeps a random 5-15 seconds to evade install-time sandbox detection. The package name and 999.0.0 version are consistent with a dependency-confusion lure targeting an internal package name.
